tail_analysis.note: 30 tasks with k15 cross-regret>0.04 are the tasks where the reproduced answer scored LOW vs this judge draw (0.402 vs 0.624 for the rest); spearman(cross_regret_k15, repro_judge_score)=-0.617; spearman(cross_regret_k15, live cohort-relative)=-0.108 (n=47, null/wrong sign) -> tail is GT-draw disagreement, not a live selection defect.

summary.conclusion: GENERATION IS THE BOTTLENECK, NOT SELECTION. Naive single-draw oracle regret +0.079 mean (median +0.027) is overfit to the judge draw: cross-draw-validated regret is -0.041 mean (median -0.070) unconstrained, and +0.009 mean / -0.021 median / improved 43 vs degraded 74 for a realistic k>=15 oracle; oracle picks overlap only 0.23 (Jaccard) between judge halves. Decomposition names no fixable mechanism: 56% of oracle tags were already in our selected 20, and the excluded ones were dropped by rank-against-our-centroid, i.e. centroid/draw noise (perfect-centroid ceiling is a known +0.0036). Our answers score 0.565 vs the judge tags own mean-cos 0.554 - selection already sits at the geometry''s natural level.
